amendments.title: The name: <app><user><distributor>, 51 lowercase base-36 characters, lossless and provably collision-free, within web SQLite's 54-character limit
amendments.rule:
Root cause confirmed: wa-sqlite's VFS declares mxPathname = 64 (expo-sqlite/web/wa-sqlite/VFS.js:10) and SQLite refuses to open when strlen(path) + 8 > mxPathname, so the databasePath expo-sqlite web passes — './' + name (SQLiteModule.ts:403 defaultDatabaseDirectory '.', pathUtils createDatabasePath) — must be <= 56: names of <= 54 open, 55+ fail with sqlite3_open_v2 (diag-04: 56 opens, 57 fails). The 199952b names are 92-96.

FORMAT: `<app><user><distributor>`, exactly 51 characters, [0-9a-z] only, no separators, no extension.
- <app>: one letter from a table in engine.ts: dos-sales -> s, dos-delivery -> d, dos-warehouse -> w, dos-harness -> h; any other prefix throws. The apps' storePrefix props and legacyStoreName(prefix) = '<prefix>.db' are unchanged.
- <user>, <distributor>: each id's 128-bit value in base 36, zero-padded to 25 digits (36^25 > 2^128 > 36^24). BUILD: the id must match /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i (canonical UUID; anything else throws — every id in this system is a UUID and a file name never carries an unchecked string), lowercase, drop hyphens, BigInt('0x'+hex).toString(36).padStart(25,'0'). PARSE: parseStoreName(name) matches /^([sdwh])([0-9a-z]{25})([0-9a-z]{25})$/, each 25-digit group back through base 36 to 32 hex digits, re-hyphenated 8-4-4-4-12; exported from engine.ts and shared.ts; docs/27 §2 carries a one-line `node -e` decode for QA listings. Example (dos_qa rahul at Tarsun): s80j3azqcg6our25a35rhwbg7r03guzv9zghwmmy1imsvb8cmft. Hermes has BigInt (RN >= 0.70); if the first Android run finds typeof BigInt === 'undefined', the builder does the base-36 division on four 32-bit limbs — the format is the rule, not the arithmetic.
- FIT: './' + 51 = 53 <= 56 on web (margin 3; the only thing that can eat it is expo-sqlite's own defaultDatabaseDirectory, pinned at 57.0.2 in the catalog); 51 of 255 bytes on Android and iOS.
- PROOF (no hash anywhere): canonical UUID <-> 128-bit integer is a bijection; 128-bit integer -> 25-digit zero-padded base-36 string is injective; the alphabet has one case, so no case-folding filesystem (the iOS simulator's container sits on a case-insensitive macOS volume) can identify two distinct names; fixed widths make the concatenation unambiguous. Hence (app, userId, tenantId) -> name is injective on every store we run (OPFS pool header byte-compare, ext4/f2fs, APFS). Amendment (a) stands with this format.
- FILES UNDER THE 199952b NAMES: on web none ever existed (the open failed before a header was written) — nothing to do. On the QA phones the long name is exported as interimStoreName(prefix, identity) and the provider's legacy effect (react.tsx:165) sweeps it ONCE for the signed-in identity with the sibling-sweep rule — deleted when it holds nothing queued/sending/refused, kept and logged ('offline: kept the store from before ruling 2') when it does — through a generalised static SyncEngine.sweepStores(storeFactory, names, onLog) that sweepIdentityStores now calls. The legacy '<prefix>.db' keeps its plain destroy (amendment i). No customer device has either name (pre-release).
- DOCS: docs/27 §2 line 40 and §13 test 12, frontend/libs/offline/README.md line 45; docs/22 §8 row handed to the main session.

amendments.title: The fallback is loud, the status names it, and a browser that cannot keep never offers to keep — the sign-out waits
amendments.rule:
- SyncStore gains `readonly fallback?: { wanted: StoreKind; reason: string }`; createMemoryStore(fallback?) carries it. open.web.ts returns the memory store with the reason 'not cross-origin isolated (no COOP/COEP)', 'no OPFS', 'expo-sqlite did not load' or 'open failed: <message>'; open.native.ts with 'expo-sqlite is not in this binary' or 'open failed: <message>'. Never silent again.
- start(): after the open, when !store.persistent && this.options.identity !== undefined, onLog('offline: no persistent store; running in memory', { name, fallback }) once. SyncStatus gains `storeNote: string | null` (the reason; null on a persistent store).
- Screens: the sales beat line s0.notPersisted and the delivery/warehouse 'Held in memory only' lines stay; the strip is unchanged (the kit's ConnectionState has no persistence field and (j) forbids a kit change — S-row).
- THE SHEET on a memory store (persistent === false): useLeaveSession exposes `persistent`; a pure leaveButtons({ mode, online, persistent }) in each app's leave.ts decides the buttons and leave-sheet.tsx renders from it: persistent -> as today; memory + online -> 'Send now', 'Cancel'; memory + offline -> 'Cancel' only. The sign-out WAITS. This follows answer A directly: the app throws nothing away; a discard verb at sign-out stays forbidden by (f); refused ops are discarded in the tray as today (orders/attention.tsx:99), and the browser that cannot keep says so. One new string, byte-identical in the three strings.ts, 'leave.bodyMemory': 'This browser cannot keep them once you leave. Send them now while there is a signal — without one, stay signed in until there is. Anything refused can be fixed or discarded in Needs attention.' leaveSentence takes `persistent` and uses this body for both modes; title and attention line unchanged. A distributor switch on a memory store is the same case (the old engine's memory dies with it), so 'Switch anyway' is withheld the same way.
- docs/27 §2 (the memory adapter is announced in the log and the status) and §12 (a store that cannot keep never offers to; the sign-out waits for a signal or the tray).

Red today: createMemoryStore takes no argument, SyncStore has no fallback, SyncStatus has no storeNote, and start() logs nothing.

amendments.title: An order and its lines are queued as one write, whole or not at all; a kept file keeps its drafts and the sweep runs on every sign-out
amendments.rule:
- Engine: enqueueMany(inputs: readonly EnqueueInput[]): Promise<string[]> — one requireStore() gate (m1), every input's shape and writable checked BEFORE anything is written (one bad line refuses the whole order), one inHand (m2), ONE store.transaction inserting the outbox rows in call order (ascending seq, header first, so FIFO still delivers the header before its lines and applyLineSync never sees a line before its order) and applying each locally, then one refreshCounts, one emit of every table touched plus OUTBOX_CHANNEL, one flush(). enqueue(input) becomes (await enqueueMany([input]))[0]. useOutbox() exposes enqueueMany.
- useEnqueueOrder (frontend/sales-app/src/lib/queue.ts:42-72) builds the header and its lines and calls enqueueMany once. OUTCOME: the phone and the office hold the whole order or none of it — refused at the gate, the rep sees the sentence of (v) and nothing is queued; past the gate, end() waits for it, counts it and keeps the file (m2, m3). A header-only draft can no longer come from a sign-out (S-120). Delivery and warehouse already queue one op per fact (deliveries carries its lines inline; receipts, trip_stops, pick_lines are single facts) — no change. Upload batching (<= 50 ops, DOS-056 bytes) is untouched.
- leaveNow (the three apps' leave.ts): LeaveSteps.end returns Promise<{ kept: boolean } | void>; kept = result?.kept ?? keepQueue. The sibling sweep runs on EVERY sign-out (it deletes only files with nothing unsent — merge review minor 2); forgetDrafts runs only when !kept, so a file kept by the re-count keeps that person's drafts with it (they are keyed by userId; nobody else can read them).
- docs/27 §6: 'an aggregate (an order and its lines) is queued in one transaction through enqueueMany'; §13 test 13 gains the case.

tests.redBecause: (1) engine started, `const ending = engine.end({ keepQueue: false })`, then enqueueMany([header, line]) rejects with { name: 'SyncEngineEndedError' } and _outbox is empty; (2) a line for a download-only table refuses the call before any write: _outbox empty and no local sales_orders row; (3) three ops land with ascending seq in call order, exactly one OUTBOX_CHANNEL emit, status().pending === 3. Red today: enqueueMany does not exist (TypeError), and the verifier's PROBE-3 shape (header resolved, line refused) is what the sequential enqueue gives.

Red today: leaveNow ignores the result and calls forgetDrafts whenever keepQueue is false, and skips the sweep whenever keepQueue is true (leave.ts:163-175).

amendments.title: The refusal reaches the sales order screen in its own words — ruling 1's optional (q), mandatory now
amendments.rule: As ruling 1 wrote it: toApiError (frontend/libs/api-client/src/errors.ts:175) maps an error whose name === 'SyncEngineEndedError' (structural check, no import of @dos/offline; amendment h stands) to new ApiError({ kind: 'auth', message: err.message, cause: err }), so orders/new.tsx:427-429 shows 'This phone is signing out; nothing more can be saved on it. Sign in again and enter it once more.' instead of 'Something could not be completed. Try again.' (web V5E, S-122). Delivery and warehouse already show the engine's sentence. The guarantee in (m) does not depend on it; the re-proof asserts the exact sentence, which also proves the gate — not some other error — refused the write.

tests.name: DOS-167 an engine that is signing out reaches the screen as a sign-in-again error in its own words
tests.redBecause: toApiError(Object.assign(new Error('This phone is signing out; nothing more can be saved on it. Sign in again and enter it once more.'), { name: 'SyncEngineEndedError', code: 'ended' })) must have kind 'auth' and that exact message. Red today: kind 'unknown', message 'Something could not be completed. Try again.'

amendments.title: The count stays as ops: S-121 remains open (P3) and the re-proof expects '2 changes' for a one-line order
amendments.rule: '2 changes have not reached the office' and '2 waiting to send' for one order with one line are true to the outbox and are NOT a DOS-167 guarantee. A user-level count needs a group_id column on _outbox (stamped by enqueueMany; the sheet and the strip count COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(group_id, op_id))), which is a device-schema bump and belongs with DOS-046's systemSchema in lean-libs-offline-boot. Out of scope here; the re-proof EXPECTS '2 changes have not reached the office' and '2 waiting to send' for one order with one line, '11' for ten lines.

docs/22 §8 row (main session's file): replace the 2026-09-13 quote 'Sign out, keep them here' with 'Sign out, keep here', add the (m) clause, and add the 2026-09-14 row from this ruling's Lane section.
summaryForFounder: The web version stopped keeping anything on the device because the file name the fix gave each person was too long for the browser's database, and the app hid that failure, so a rep could be told his unsent order was kept when it was not; the phone versions were fine. The repair gives the file a short name that still says exactly whose it is and which distributor it belongs to, makes the app say out loud when it cannot keep anything, and in that case never offers to keep — it asks the rep to send now or stay signed in until there is a signal. An order and its lines are now saved together or not at all, and a rep refused because the phone is signing out is told so in plain words; the count on the sign-out screen still counts an order and each of its lines separately, which is left for a later fix.
notes:
Written: /Users/prajwalchavan/Desktop/Distribution OS/QA/evidence/batch2/verdicts/DOS-167-ruling-2.md (under 150 lines). Read-only otherwise; no build, test, git write or database connection; worktrees untouched.

Why this format and not a shorter hash: only a case-insensitive alphabet makes the injectivity proof hold on every filesystem we run (the iOS simulator's container is on a case-insensitive macOS volume), and base 36 is the densest such alphabet made of safe characters: 25 digits per UUID, 51 with the app letter, './'+51 = 53 <= 56. Base64url would give 45-48 characters but is only injective on case-sensitive stores; base32 (52) and hex (64) do not fit. Exactness: the SQLite rule is nPathname + 8 <= mxPathname (64) with wa-sqlite's mxPathname, so the databasePath may be 56 and a name 54; the task's '54+ fail' is off by one against diag-04 (56 opens, 57 fails); the ruling uses the measured numbers.

Why the memory-store sign-out WAITS (needsFounder false): answer A says nothing is thrown away and (f) forbids a discard verb at sign-out; a browser that cannot keep has no 'keep' to offer, so the only honest offers are Send now (online) and staying signed in (offline), with the tray for refusals. The founder's objection to 'refuse until sent' was about a shared PHONE in a dead spot; on a non-persistent browser the queue dies with the tab whatever the app does, and the session-handover risk is the refresh token's, which is unchanged by either choice. The founder may reword leave.bodyMemory; the three facts (no keep on a memory store, Send now only online, the sign-out waits) are the rule.

Rating: (s) is the P0's own regression (S-123, P1 on web); (t) is what turns a silent broken promise into an honest one; (u) closes S-120 and merge-review minor 2; (v) closes S-122. One lane over main (199952b+), test-first in the order s -> t -> u -> v -> docs, then the re-proof, then my merge review. Sizing: engine/name/openers 0.3 d, apps' leave.ts/sheet/strings 0.2 d, enqueueMany + queue.ts 0.15 d, docs 0.05 d, re-proof web 0.25 d, Android 0.3 d (sales 1-6 + upgrade + delivery/warehouse 1-3), iOS 0.15 d.
